content.thinking:
I'm planning the capybara's proportions and whimsical design, then working out the skeleton structure starting with hips and spine chain, plus a small bird perched on its head.

Defining joint hierarchy...

Working out the leg chains next—front legs bend elbows backward while hind legs bend knees forward, with hip and foot positions chosen so segment lengths comfortably span the distance. I'm naming the joint chains for each limb (shoulder/elbow/hand, hip/knee/foot), parenting front legs to the spine and hind legs to the hips, and setting slightly thicker sweep radii to keep that chubby capybara build.

Now I'm defining toes as small spheres or a simple box foot, and sorting out the side convention—since local +X reads as right but world +X is actually left, I'm treating positive x as the "L" side using literal coordinates. For the body itself, I'm building a loft along a catmull path running from rump to chest, bound to the spine bone chain, with control points placed to shape the torso's curve.

For the radius profile along that sweep, I'm using an array of four keys with rounded end caps, tying the bone list through the hips and spine. For coloring, I'm layering fur textures: a mottled brown/tan countershaded coat with a lighter belly tone, then wrapping it in a cel-shading pass to get a toon-like look, confirming the nesting of cel over the lit paint works correctly.

I'm keeping fur detail modest—just a scatter of about 120 small tuft cards across the back of the body using a filter on vertical position, with a single SVG tuft shape and a brownish color string, rendered double-sided on the body surface.

For the head, I'm blocking out capybara anatomy: a scaled skull sphere, a frustum-shaped muzzle box tapering from wider at the base to narrower near the tip, attached to the head bone, with a flat-ended upper section that I'll round off with a nose piece.

Now adding the nose as a dark boxy sphere, a lower jaw frustum tapering similarly in tan, a thin dark mouth line, whimsically oversized dark eyes with small white highlight specs using low-poly spheres, rounded brown ears with pink inner color, and tiny dark nostril spheres positioned just below the nose.

Next I'm placing the nose pad sphere right at the muzzle's end, adding a few thin whisker rods per side, and cream buck-teeth boxes tucked under the nose on the jaw front, while keeping the total color count under 64. Then I'm starting a whimsical round bluebird perched on top of the head, building its body as a scaled sphere positioned just above the head surface.

Adding wing joint placement with small scaled sphere parts, blue body with cream belly and orange accents, and little whimsical touches like dark toenail boxes and a tiny yellow flower tucked behind the ear for charm.

For the flower I'm placing five small petal spheres around a center point on the head bone, skipping a complicated mouth sweep in favor of a simple dark rod line across the muzzle, and adding toe boxes as tiny spheres clustered at each foot position.

Now I'm attaching nails to the actual tip joint of each leg since that's where the three-joint chain ends, adding a dark foot pad sphere sized to sit flush with the floor, and checking that the leg tube's rounded cap doesn't sink the foot too far below ground level—it's slightly over so I need to adjust the foot target position.

I'm adjusting leg target heights and radii so the capped tube bottoms meet the pads correctly, lengthening the front and hind limb segments slightly so they stay bent naturally rather than overextending, and confirming the body's radius keeps the belly sitting above the legs. Now I'm working out the neck sweep radii and starting the neck path coordinates where it joins the head.

Still defining skeleton geometry...

I'll scatter the fur tufts across the body surface, leaning them at an angle with varied sizes, aiming for roughly 140 tufts each made of a few triangles. For imports, I need to be careful to only bring in what's actually used—THREE, builder, catmull, limb, rng, cel, svg, countershade, mottle—and define a hit filter that keeps only upward-facing normals. Now I'm figuring out how limb's returned points feed into the chain path, checking whether a plain array works as a polyline input.

Polylines work fine since sweeps round the corners naturally, so I'll build each leg chain with the correct parent joint—hips for hind legs, the third spine joint for front legs. For limb bends, front legs get the elbow bending backward while hind legs need the knee bending forward to mimic a quadruped's stifle-then-hock structure. Then I'm writing the sweep calls for each leg, using a two-value radius array for taper and assigning the coat color.

For the ears, I'm placing small flattened dark-brown spheres near the top of the skull with tiny pink inner spheres for detail. For the eyes, I'm calculating exactly where they sit on the skull ellipsoid's curved surface so they look properly embedded rather than floating, working out the x-position using the ellipsoid's radii along each axis—landing around x=0.093 with a 0.028 radius, going for a glossy black eye look.

Adding a tiny white sparkle offset toward the front-upper edge of each eye for that glossy highlight. For the muzzle, I'm building a tapered box frustum shape from the skull down to a narrower front, sized to sit just below the skull's top curve, then placing a large dark oval nose pad at the front tip—skipping separate nostril details for now to keep things simple.

Adjusting jaw dimensions so it sits correctly against the muzzle without a gap, then adding cream incisor boxes, whisker rods angling from cheek outward, and considering a cheek blush decal for extra detail.

Skipping hip tail nub and bird feet since the bird sits fluffy on the head without visible legs, and instead adding a tail feather as a frustum box angled back and up from the bird's body to give it shape.

Placing more bird details now, working out the body sphere, head sphere, beak position, eyes, cream chest patch, crest spikes, and wing joints, then defining the skeletal joints connecting birdBody to birdHead...

Adding flower petals near the head...
